title: record page: an Edit disabled by userActions.edit.disabledWhen gives no reason, unlike the state and approval locks
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbabAdcWyApSTGBYJNY

Filing category: out-of-scope finding from the dev of objectstack#35099 (draft PR #35133, Acceptance notes), filed by the seat. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What is missing

When an object's `userActions.edit.disabledWhen` holds, the record page shows Edit as off (`aria-disabled="true"`) and says nothing about why, on desktop and on the phone alike. The other two disable reasons do say why: the state lock draws its `record-state-lock` badge ("Not editable in its current state"), and the approval lock has its band.

Cause: `userActions.edit` declares `enabled` / `visibleWhen` / `disabledWhen` and no reason key, so the console has no text to show.

## What it would take

A readable reason needs a new authorable key beside `disabledWhen` (e.g. a localized reason string), so `Metadata-protocol: added` and a contract review. The key's name and shape, and whether a generic fallback text is enough instead, are open; decide them when the card is picked up (key names are PM discretion unless they diverge from an existing pattern).

## Done when

- A `disabledWhen`-disabled Edit shows a reason a reader can see on desktop and on the phone (tooltip or inline, matching the state-lock badge), or the card records why a generic text is enough.
- Pins on both faces.
